title: Two Roads to Causal Attention
objective: See that lines 62-71 compute causal attention in one of two ways, depending on `self.flash`. One way is a single fused call. The other is a manual sequence: score, mask the future, softmax, then mix the values.
audience_context: The learner is in the tokenization part of the material. They pointed at model.py:62-71 inside CausalSelfAttention.forward, where q, k and v already exist and get combined into y.
scope_note: I left out the dropout details (`self.attn_dropout`, `dropout_p`), tensor shapes (B, nh, T, hs), why the Flash kernels are faster, and the PyTorch version check. These are minor or optional (C5, C6). Ten seconds is enough for the fork and the four manual steps.

evidence.excerpt:
# flash attention make GPU go brrrrr but support is only in PyTorch >= 2.0
        self.flash = hasattr(torch.nn.functional, 'scaled_dot_product_attention')

# causal mask to ensure that attention is only applied to the left in the input sequence
            self.register_buffer("bias", torch.tril(torch.ones(config.block_size, config.block_size))
                                        .view(1, 1, config.block_size, config.block_size))

else:
            # manual implementation of attention
            att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))
            att = att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))
            att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)
            att = self.attn_dropout(att)
            y = att @ v # (B, nh, T, T) x (B, nh, T, hs) -> (B, nh, T, hs)

branches.runs: model.py:62-64: y = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None, dropout_p=self.dropout if self.training else 0, is_causal=True)

claim_registry.text: When `self.flash` is true, y comes from a single call: `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None, dropout_p=self.dropout if self.training else 0, is_causal=True)`. The manual lines are skipped.

When `self.flash` is false, the manual path first computes scores: `att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))`. That is the query-key dot products, scaled by 1/sqrt of the head size.

On the `self.flash`-false branch, the next step is `att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))`. It sets scores to -inf wherever the lower-triangular `bias` buffer is 0, which are the future positions. As a result, each position attends only to positions on its left.
On the `self.flash`-false branch, `F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` turns each row of masked scores into weights. Future positions get weight 0. Then `y = att @ v` takes a weighted sum of the value vectors.
`self.flash` is set by checking `hasattr(torch.nn.functional, 'scaled_dot_product_attention')`. Per the code comment, that function is only available in PyTorch >= 2.0.
On the flash branch, the causal restriction is requested with `is_causal=True`, with no explicit mask (`attn_mask=None`).

must_show: A fork labeled `if self.flash:` with two branches. Only one branch lights up per pass.
Flash branch: one box labeled `scaled_dot_product_attention(... is_causal=True)` that takes q, k, v and outputs y
Manual branch: four steps in order: `q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)` scaled → `masked_fill(... float('-inf'))` → `F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` → `att @ v`
A small T×T score grid whose upper-right (future) cells turn to -inf at the mask step, then to 0 after softmax, while each row's remaining weights add up to 1
Both branches end at the same output label y
must_not_claim: That both branches run on every forward pass, or that the manual steps always run (they run only when `self.flash` is false)
That the flash call is always used
That softmax happens before masking, or that `att @ v` comes before softmax (the order is score → mask → softmax → multiply by v)
That masking deletes or removes tokens from the sequence. It only sets their scores to -inf, so their weights become 0.
That softmax normalizes over the whole matrix or over the batch. It normalizes each row (dim=-1).
That the flash path skips causal masking (it passes `is_causal=True`)
That this code performs tokenization or works on raw text
That dropout is applied on the flash path at inference time (dropout_p is 0 when not training)
visual_direction: Open on q, k, v flowing into the `self.flash` fork. Light the flash branch briefly to show one compact box producing y. Then switch to the false branch and follow the score grid as it changes: dot products fill the grid, the future triangle darkens to -inf, softmax turns each row into weights with the future cells at 0, and the weights then pull from v to make y. Keep attention on the grid as the main object. Settle at the end on the shared output y so it's clear both branches deliver the same kind of result.
